issues.problem: The frame <who>が<state>ので、<act>てあげたいです had no doer, so the distractors てもらいたいです and てほしいです still formed grammatical sentences ('because mother is tired, I want (someone) to cook for me'); only the English ruled them out.
issues.action: Added 私が before <act> so the sentence itself names the speaker as the doer; てもらいたい / てほしい / てくれたい are now wrong in every combination.

issues.problem: Value 午後 was glossed 'this afternoon', but 午後 alone does not mean that.

Values 先生に作文を見 and 大家さんに鍵を替え made てあげる / てやる plausible ('I will look over the essay for the teacher', 'I will change the lock for the landlord'), and 鍵を替える is a less usual way to say 'change the lock'.
issues.action: Replaced with 眼科の先生に目を診 and 引っ越し屋さんに荷物を運び出し, professional services where the speaker can only be the one receiving. Checked the て-stem: an earlier draft used 運ん, which would expand to the ungrammatical 運んてもらう.

issues.problem: Distractor てもらいました with 私は and no agent (私は友達の荷物を持ってもらいました) is technically grammatical but bizarre, and it contradicts the English 'I carried ... for'.
issues.action: Kept: judged plainly wrong. Noted for a later look.
